question: Will this project complete a correct, audited proof of the Four Colour Theorem along its routes: Lemma R* proved in the core class or in its weakest compiled form, the frame class (since 7 Oct: no frozen pi-orbit at some degree-5 vertex of every frame-class triangulation, via LPC), with the reduction to 4CT compiled in Lean?
by: Coordination session (Claude Opus 5.5), the coordinator's own judgement, not a ledger status

components.label: R* is true in the frame class (some degree-5 vertex has no frozen orbit; LPC, 4CT-strength, is the stronger every-vertex form)
We prove it (LPC or NoFrozenFrame on the sphere: NRC plus the mixed higher chain counts), given it is true
The formal chain closes: NoFrozenFrame => RStarFrame => 4CT for spherical maps compiled and audited (J12, J14); remaining scope gap: drawing => combinatorial map (deferred)
Separate meter: a worthwhile result (the chain-parity note, the VH-exists record paper with its Lean reduction, or a counterexample)

evidence_for: 8 Oct, formal (audit J14 PASS: clean rebuild 91/91 modules, all axioms standard, statements checked against the paper, hypotheses shown satisfiable on the 22-vertex frame witness): no frozen orbits => R* on the frame class => 4CT for spherical maps, with frozen Mathlib-only challenge statements and proved anti-drift bridges; lock parity; N >= 8 with equality exactly at rigid states; the mod-4 chain-count formula (Conjecture F, via Tutte's identity); the chain-parity law; rigid isolation; Remark 7.

8 Oct: the chain-parity law and rigid isolation are the first planarity-dependent theorems that hold at every degree-5 hole of the frame class (earlier theorems H, HP, F5, weak F6 only at diamond holes, which never occur there). They fail on the torus, Klein bottle and RP2, as a proof must. The law has two independently reviewed hand proofs (curve surgery; Tutte + Fisk) as well as the Lean proof.

8 Oct, hand, independently reviewed (not formal): J1-J5 and the sigma-type lemma pin a near-rigid frozen class to 20-state cycles alternating 8, 9 chains, so LPC splits into named cases: rigid (excluded, formal), constant N (excluded, formal), alternating 8,9 (NRC, open), mixed higher counts (open).

Data (exploratory, not audit-replayed): exhaustive frame-class census to order 34 (about 3.9e9 plantri graphs, 289,827 frame-class graphs, 4.95M holes): R* at every degree-5 vertex, quarter floor met exactly and never broken, lock parity 0 failures (1.59e9 states at order 34), NRC holds (no near-rigid cycle; max near-rigid run flat at 8 over orders 33-34, a cycle needs 10); all 98 all-DL pi-cycles at order 34 sit in classes with filled states. LPC: no counterexample on five other surfaces (1.11M evaluations).

N1 (data with exact certificates): law-respecting near-rigid cycles off the sphere always need at least one extra edge; e = 0 proved infeasible (CP-SAT + HiGHS with LP certificates) for the three minimal skeletons.

7 Oct morning: 51 sorry-free Lean modules (regression 75/75): Theorem W, F5, flow identity, assignment and budget certificates (BudgetUnionPos => floor => R* => 4CT), time reversal, pair dualities, pocket/crossing lemmas, weak F6 (PureClean at four consecutive degree-5 neighbours). SigmaUnionC and the floor survived every adversarial search (396 walks; 61+12 constructed graphs).

7 Oct, 02:45: Theorem F5 is FORMAL (quarterFloor_of_fiveLink: the quarter floor at every hole with five degree-5 neighbours, from triangulation alone). Thirteen sorry-free Lean files: Lemma A, rotation bijection, Hex, no-frozen, Lemma Pi, Theorem W, F5, the exact sigma-exit condition, sigma-groups with sigmaC => floor. The open problem is the formal SigmaCConj on three-consecutive-5s holes, with a tested mechanism (Conjecture G) and 0 failures at those families.

Night of 6-7 Oct: Theorem W formal in Lean (3F - U = -5 x winding; floor <=> sum lambda <= 0 per class); Lemma A, rotation bijection, Hex dichotomy, no-frozen, Lemma Pi all compiled with standard axioms. Theorem F5 (hand, reviewed PASS): the quarter floor holds at every (5,5,5,5,5) hole, the first floor theorem beyond R*. Transport statement holds on all 136 classes + Studio orders 24-26, Hall ratio >= 3.

Quarter floor (exploratory, exhaustive): every Kempe class of T - v at a degree-5 vertex has >= 1/4 filled states, all 160,979 classes at orders 12-24 (419 exactly at 1/4); no such floor at degrees 6/7. The inequality U_j <= F_{j+1}+F_{j+3}+F_{j+4} holds in every class. R* becomes a counting problem.
Lemma A (Math, hand, review pending): the non-doubly-locked half of the counting inequality, by Kempe's single swap made injective (per j; Intern C review).
Historical traps: Heawood's own 1890 failing colouring refills in 2 swaps; Saaty-type HoG 1152 (3-4 classes after deletion) passes at all holes.
Frame theorem four_color_of_RStarFrame compiled (Studio Math, merged b4b617d): R* only for core graphs with no Birkhoff diamond and no 2.122 implies 4CT; audit J12 pending.

Historical traps pass: Errera (17) and Kittell (23) are core-class graphs; every degree-5 hole fills within 4 swaps, no stuck class (but T - v has one class there, so this re-checks colourability, not R*).
four_color_of_core_Rstar compiles: core-class R* in its exact hand form implies every planar map is 4-colourable (audit pending).
Link D compiles end to end: four_color_of_RStarSupport (core-class R* => every planar map 4-colourable), standard axioms, audit pending.
The reduction R* => VH_C => VH-exists => 4CT is proved by hand and re-derived by the audit.
Compiled and audited in Lean: Euler lemma (both forms), Theorem H, Theorem HP, and R* (global form) => 4CT.
R* holds whenever at most one neighbour of the hole has degree >= 6 (H, HP).
No targetless class anywhere: WP20 P1 (all 25,381 order-25 graphs, reproduced on a second machine), WP21, and the pre-registered adversary searches.
Route B (small computer-checked Kempe-reducible set) opened as a second path to R*.
Math claims [unreviewed] R* at every hole with three consecutive degree-5 neighbours (covers T4's class and two radius-5 classes); review and machine test running.
Every hard graph found so far (106 graphs, 500 radius-4/5 holes) contains the Birkhoff diamond or RSST configuration 2.122, both classically reducible; large-graph test running.
evidence_against: 8 Oct, the NRC wall: seven consecutive attempts on NRC (Tracks L, N, P, Q, R, S, T) produced structure but no proof; Euler counting, LP duality, Laman, monotone quantities and chord/interlace statistics are all insufficient, and T1 is false (a non-planar n = 22 law-respecting closed orbit), so NRC needs a second planar input beyond the law. New attacks are paused.

The case of LPC with mixed higher chain counts (N >= 10 on cycles) is untouched and has no handle; LPC itself is Tilley's D-resolvability at every degree-5 vertex (as far as we can tell), so it is at least as strong as 4CT.

Killed 7-8 Oct: a small unavoidable set of hole types (59 optimal for one-step rules, 66666 forced, no type with PureClean proved), G66 by multi-hole compensation, the Barnette signed sum, a stream function, any hole-local proof of LPC (a 28-vertex non-planar counterexample satisfies every local fact), R <= 5, N1+ (e >= 2), T1, QC.

Census trends: max interior run R jumps 6 -> 8 at order 34; holes at the maximal near-rigid run rise 1 -> 5 and NR = 7 holes 11 -> 43; all-DL pi-cycles grow faster than holes (25 -> 98). The census is consistent with truth, not evidence of provability, and covers orders <= 34 only.

7 Oct morning: the per-cycle chain (A34', W2, Lemma S_Gamma) and statement (c)/IB-N0 are false at degree 6 on constructed graphs (Studio Jobs AW, BV); weak F6 lies in Birkhoff-diamond (reducible) territory, so it does not move 4CT; no forcing mechanism for the group statements was found; the frontier G66 (all-6 holes) is non-local (2-ball silent) and DL runs grow with fullerene size.

7 Oct: universal sigma-C is false (one island group at a (5,6,5,6,6) hole); Conjecture G fails off the three families; Conjecture P (configurations) false in both regimes. The general case still needs lock-breaking swaps of other colour pairs and remains 4CT-strength.

Night of 6-7 Oct: floor and R* fail massively on the torus (frozen classes from n=16), so the proof must use the sphere; no single-cycle bound (w=+160 exists); per-state Euler counts, charges, Gauss-Bonnet shape, per-path charging, identity induction and closed-set descent all fail; the configuration and link-pattern leads were base-rate effects. The general DL-half remains 4CT-strength.
The open (doubly locked) half of the quarter-floor inequality is as strong as R* at every degree-5 vertex (Tilley's conjecture); Lemma A is purely local and contains no global step.

Math (16:15): no mechanism by which diamond-freeness helps a Kempe argument; the exclusions remove exactly the degree-5 vertices that confine chains. Configuration-free core graphs are very rare below order 32 (1, 1, 4, 2 at orders 22-25), so 'no radius >= 4 without a diamond' rests on few graphs.

Outside advisor (SageAdvice-2026-10-06.md): R* is strictly stronger than 4CT, the induction gives no leverage on Kempe classes, no invariant separates classes; data consistent with truth is not evidence of provability. Estimate 0.1-0.5%.
Radius-versus-order census (exhaustive, no separating triangles): max radius 3 at orders 12-19, 4 at 20-21, 5 at 22-25. Still rising.

The vertex property R* needs is (as far as we can tell) Tilley's D-resolvability (JGAA 2017); Tilley's published open conjecture (every degree-5 vertex) implies R* (one vertex per graph), so R* is a weaker but still open statement in a recognised line of work.

Route B as a pure vacancy set is dead: on the RSST configurations, vacancy-reducibility is weaker than classical D-reducibility (8 of the first 11 classically reducible configurations fail at every degree-5 vertex).
Radius 5 confirmed in the core by the audit's replay (three distinct states); 13 more radius-5 graphs found; radius grows with order.
Every local route so far has died: link classes, 2-balls, the 74-pattern automaton, Conjecture L, fixed radius bounds.
The open case is where Kempe's 1879 argument failed; every known proof needs hundreds of reducible configurations.
The audit judges R* at least as strong as VH-exists: the reduction sharpened the target but did not shrink it.
Literature check: no source states R*; it may be false.

Navigator revision 143: night's results recorded; probability unchanged (formal infrastructure up, but the per-cycle routes died and the surviving statements have no mechanism).

Navigator revision 144 (coordinator's estimate): the reduction NoFrozenFrame => R* => 4CT and the first planarity-dependent invariants at every frame-class hole (lock parity, chain-count formula, chain-parity law, rigid isolation) are compiled and audited (J14), and LPC is split into named cases. Prove factor 3% -> 4%. Held back by the NRC wall (seven attempts, no proof) and the untouched mixed higher counts.
